My Dad ran a clothing manufacturing operation all his life. The oversizes were the absolute worst. Not only did you have to grade the patterns to the extra sizes but you had to stock the garments as well. In a commercial manufacturing operation you never make just one of a size, like you would if you're a tailor. The minimum run of one size of a certain style was 12. So that means you put into inventory at least 12 each of XXXL, XXXXL, all the way up to XXXXXXXL (that's 7 Xs). Not to mention the style may also have regular, short, and tall lengths for each size, which triples the inventory right there.

So for that 3 times a year he'd get an order for a XXXXXXXL he'd have to make and carry many times that in stock. Now multiply it by literally hundreds of styles in a minimum of 3 colors usually 5 and you have a shit tonne of inventory that turns over very slowly, which btw is a killer in the garment trade.

So when he charged double for the extreme oversizes it wasn't because he was a greedy shitlord. It was because he was trying to provide a service to customers and not go out of business in the process.
